mcq.question: Why does `Length<Metres>{1} + Length<Feet>{3}` fail to compile?

options.C: They are different types and `operator+` is only defined for two lengths of the same unit

mcq.explanation: Encoding the unit in the type lets the compiler reject unit mix-ups. A deliberate conversion such as `to_metres` is required.

mcq.question: When should you choose `std::variant` over `std::any`?

options.A: When the set of possible types is known and fixed, so the compiler can check that every case is handled
options.B: When values may be of any type that plugins invent later
options.C: When you want to avoid all type checks

mcq.explanation: A variant's alternatives are part of its type, and `std::visit` must handle each one. `std::any` accepts unknown types but checks them only when `any_cast` is called.

bonus.question: Dynamic languages check types at run time; C++ checks most of them at compile time. Which bugs in this spreadsheet engine would a dynamically typed version only find in production?
Write a failing test for a new `Date` alternative in `Cell` (text like `2026-04-30`). Add it and let the compiler show every visitor you must update.
